'''Coralia Cartis''' is a Romanian mathematician at the [[University of Oxford]] whose research interests include [[compressed sensing]], [[numerical analysis]], and [[Regularization (mathematics)|regularisation]] methods in [[mathematical optimization]].<!-- Note that her publications spell regularisation with an s and optimization with a z. Is this a consistent national variety of English? Who knows but it's the variety she uses. --> At Oxford, she is a Professor in Numerical Optimization in the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]], and a tutorial fellow of [[Balliol College, Oxford|Balliol College]].{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Born in [[Cluj-Napoca]], [[Romania]],{{r|floreat}} Cartis earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Babeș-Bolyai University]],{{r|turing}} and completed her PhD in 2005 at the [[University of Cambridge]]. Her dissertation, ''On Interior Point Methods for Linear Programming'', was supervised by [[Michael J. D. Powell]].{{r|mg}} In the same year, she was one of the Second Prize winners of the [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]].{{r|fox}}

After working as a researcher at the [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] and a postdoctoral researcher at Oxford, she became a lecturer at the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 2007. She took her present position at Oxford in 2013.{{r|turing}}

In 2018 she became a member of the scientific board of the Smith Institute for Industrial Mathematics and System Engineering,{{r|smith}} and was a plenary speaker at the 16th EUROPT Workshop on Advances in Continuous Optimization in Spain.{{r|europt}}

Cartis was elected to the 2023 Class of [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] Fellows.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIAM Announces Class of 2023 Fellows |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2023-fellows |access-date=2023-04-08 |website=SIAM News |date=30 March 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref>
